name: Pearl Millet
harvestProduct: dry grain (whole plant also used as fodder/silage)

evidence.quote: It is generally sensitive to low temperatures at the seedling stage and at flowering.

frostTender.notes: Source describes cold sensitivity but does not state an explicit frost-kill temperature; corroborated by FAO ECOCROP's killing temperature (KTMP = 0 degC) for Pennisetum glaucum.

evidence.quote: Pearl millet is propagated by seed.
Optimum planting time should be early October to November, and this is greatly dependent on the intended use.
Pearl millet usually flowers from 40 to 55 days.
The seed begins developing after fertilisation and matures 25 to 30 days later.

daysToHarvestRange.notes: Computed as flowering (40-55 days from planting) plus grain maturation (25-30 days after flowering) = 65-85 days to grain maturity. Source separately notes 'Grain can be harvested as early as 40 days after flowering' (p.7 of the guideline / page 13 of PDF) as a minimum-moisture early-harvest option.

zoneNotes.lowveld-bushveld: Limpopo is named as a major production area.
zoneNotes.subtropical-coast: KwaZulu-Natal is named as a major production area.
zoneNotes.highveld: Free State is named as a major production area, alongside the crop's stated sensitivity to low temperatures at seedling and flowering stages.

gaps: 'No known varieties have been developed in South Africa to date.' -- direct quote from the source; varieties list is empty because none exist to cite.

No row spacing, in-row spacing, or numeric sowing-depth figures given -- only 'shallow planting is recommended' (non-numeric) and a plant-density figure of 100 000 to 175 000 plants/ha ('similar or slightly higher... than for sorghum').
No yield figure: the source explicitly states 'There are no records with regard to the size of land under production and the quantities produced' for South Africa.
No winter-rainfall, all-year, or mild-frost specific sowing windows; only one national window given.
No explicit frost-kill temperature stated in the DAFF guideline (inferred cold sensitivity + FAO ECOCROP KTMP=0 used instead).
summary: DAFF's 2011 Pearl Millet production guideline gives a sowing window and a days-to-maturity figure that can be computed from its flowering/seed-maturation data, but has no row/in-row spacing, sowing depth, seed rate, or yield figures, and explicitly states no SA varieties exist and no production/area records are kept. Verdict is partial, held back mainly by the missing spacing and yield data required for 'ready'.
